# RouteWise MSA — required redlines

These five edits address the playbook's hard rules. Section 10.1 already survives under §12.3. The DPA edit requires a completed Exhibit C to be attached and executed at signing; wording alone does not cure the missing exhibit.

## 1. IP indemnity and liability cap — A1

Replace §§9.1 and 9.3 with:

> **9.1** Except for the liabilities excluded from limitation under Section 9.3, neither party's aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
>
> **9.3** The exclusions and limitations in this Section 9, including the cap in Section 9.1 and the damages exclusion in Section 9.2, shall not apply to Provider's obligations under Section 10.1; either party's liability for its gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; or Customer's payment obligations. Provider's obligations under Section 10.1 are uncapped and survive expiration or termination as provided in Section 12.3.

The current §9.1 begins “notwithstanding anything to the contrary,” which can control the “uncapped” language in §10.1. [Interpretation authority](../library/contract_interpretation_notwithstanding.md).

## 2. Executed data processing addendum — A2

Replace §5.3 with:

> **5.3** The data processing addendum attached as Exhibit C is incorporated into this Agreement and shall be executed by both parties at the same time as this Agreement. Provider shall not process personal data of EU or UK residents on Customer's behalf unless and until the executed Exhibit C is in effect. The parties shall complete Exhibit C so that it specifies the subject matter and duration, nature and purpose of processing, categories of personal data and data subjects, and the parties' obligations and rights, including the processor obligations required by Article 28(3) of the GDPR where applicable.

Replace the placeholder Exhibit C with the negotiated, completed, signed DPA before signature. The [library's Article 28 excerpt](../library/gdpr_art28.md) identifies the required processor terms.

## 3. Initial and renewal pricing — A3

Replace Exhibit A, §4 (Pricing adjustments) with:

> **4. Pricing adjustments.** Fees stated in this Order Form are fixed for the entire Initial Subscription Term; Provider may not increase them during that term. For each renewal term, Provider may increase the fees once, effective only at the start of that renewal term, by no more than the lesser of five percent (5%) or the percentage increase in the CPI-U over the preceding twelve (12) months. If the CPI-U has not increased, no renewal increase is permitted. Provider must give Customer written notice of any proposed renewal increase at least ninety (90) days before the renewal term begins. In the absence of timely notice, fees for that renewal term remain unchanged.

This replaces the order form's unilateral midterm increase and uncapped renewal language. The order form controls conflicting MSA terms under §14.1.

## 4. Automatic renewal — A4

Replace §3.3 with:

> **3.3** Each Subscription Term shall automatically renew for successive terms of twelve (12) months unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term.

## 5. Affiliate license — A5

Replace §2.2 with:

> **2.2** The license and access rights granted under this Agreement and each Order Form extend to Customer and to Cobalt Freight Europe B.V. and Cobalt Brokerage LLC at no additional fee. Each such Affiliate may use the Services through its employees and contractors, who shall be deemed Users for purposes of this Agreement. Customer remains responsible for those Users' compliance with this Agreement. No separate Order Form or additional affiliate fee is required for these rights.
# RouteWise: signature decision for the COO

**Deal.** RouteWise will provide routing and fleet optimization for up to 350 vehicles. The first subscription runs 36 months from provisioning. Base fees are $18,500 per month, billed annually in advance, plus a $25,000 one-time implementation fee. Arithmetic: $18,500 × 12 = $222,000 a year; $222,000 × 3 = $666,000 for 36 months; $666,000 + $25,000 = **$691,000** before taxes and any permitted fee changes. The service target is 99.5% monthly availability, with capped service credits.

## Five changes required before signature

1. **Attach and sign a complete data processing addendum.** Exhibit C is blank, while EU driver data will run through the platform. The reference library says a binding processor contract with required terms must be in place from the first day of processing ([GDPR Article 28 excerpt](../library/gdpr_art28.md)). Do not start EU or UK personal-data processing before the completed DPA is effective.
2. **Make the vendor's IP indemnity genuinely uncapped.** The indemnity says “uncapped,” but the liability cap starts “notwithstanding anything to the contrary” and can override it ([interpretation authority](../library/contract_interpretation_notwithstanding.md)). The cap must expressly exempt the IP indemnity; its protection must survive termination.
3. **Fix pricing.** The order form allows one increase during the initial 36 months on 60 days' notice, by up to the greater of 8% or CPI-U, and leaves renewal increases uncapped. Remove the initial-term increase. Cap each renewal increase at the lower of 5% or CPI-U, with 90 days' notice. For scale, 8% of $18,500 is $1,480 more each month, or $17,760 for a full year at that rate. Actual exposure depends on CPI-U and when the increase begins.
4. **Shorten auto-renewal.** Current language rolls the subscription into another 24 months unless Cobalt gives notice 90 days in advance. Limit renewals to 12 months and require no more than 30 days' notice to opt out.
5. **Include the two named affiliates at no extra fee.** The current license expressly excludes affiliates and charges more to add them. Cover Cobalt Freight Europe B.V. and Cobalt Brokerage LLC, including their employees and contractors, under the existing order.

**Negotiable improvement.** The SLA gives credits as the sole remedy for downtime. Ask for an express right to terminate if availability misses the target in three months of any six; the general breach clause does not clearly provide that exit. This is a preferred playbook position, subject to Legal approval to concede.

**Decision.** The five required edits are hard-rule issues under Cobalt's playbook. They need to be resolved in the signed agreement, with an actual executed DPA, before approval to sign. The redline text is in `redlines.md`.
COMPLETE

Required deliverables are present: `issues.json`, `redlines.md`, and `coo_onepager.md`. No client questions were needed. The proposed DPA clause remains conditional on the parties attaching and executing a completed Exhibit C at signing; the current placeholder does not satisfy that requirement.

item.text: I found two points to tighten. The DPA redline used future tense even though the playbook requires the exhibit to be complete at signing. The COO page also described all five hard rules as absolute signing bars, although the playbook allows GC-approved waivers. I’m correcting both and will mark the missing signed DPA as an open transaction item.

item.text:
I reviewed the deliverables against the contract, playbook, and indexed library and made these corrections:

- Reworded the DPA redline so Exhibit C must be **completed and executed at signing**, rather than completed later.
- Clarified in the COO page that hard rules can be waived with GC approval, while a waiver does not replace the processor contract required before EU personal-data processing.
- Changed [STATUS.md](/work/workspace/deliverable/STATUS.md) to **COMPLETE WITH OPEN ITEMS** because the vendor draft still lacks a completed, signed DPA.
- Corrected the library paths in [issues.json](/work/workspace/deliverable/issues.json).

I validated the JSON, redline consistency, source paths, and arithmetic. No numerical discrepancy remains.
